title: International Society of Sports Nutrition position stand: caffeine and exercise performance
publisher: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
claims: Caffeine can acutely enhance various aspects of exercise performance in many but not all studies, with aerobic endurance showing the most consistent moderate-to-large benefits.
Doses of 3-6 mg/kg body mass have consistently improved exercise performance; very high doses are associated with more side effects.
A common timing is about 60 minutes before exercise, although optimal timing depends on the caffeine source.
Individual responses vary, and caffeine can adversely affect sleep or anxiety in some people.

claimVerification.note: 原文：“Supplementation with caffeine has been shown to acutely enhance various aspects of exercise performance in many but not all studies”；“Aerobic endurance appears to be the form of exercise with the most consistent moderate-to-large benefits from caffeine use”。

原文：“Caffeine has consistently been shown to improve exercise performance when consumed in doses of 3–6 mg/kg body mass”；“Very high doses of caffeine (e.g. 9 mg/kg) are associated with a high incidence of side-effects”。
原文：“The most commonly used timing of caffeine supplementation is 60 min pre-exercise. Optimal timing of caffeine ingestion likely depends on the source of caffeine.”

原文：“Inter-individual differences in sport and exercise performance as well as adverse effects on sleep or feelings of anxiety following caffeine ingestion may be attributed to genetic variation… Other factors such as habitual caffeine intake also may play a role”。
